title: Rencontre à la salle de sport  (Meeting at the Gym)

segments.t: At an exclusive Parisian fitness club, Andrea tracks down renowned actor Fabrice Luchini on the workout machines. She delivers a passionate pitch to poach him for the ASK agency, but Luchini has his own unique philosophy. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Bonjour, Fabrice! Tu viens souvent ici?
Je vous connais, vous êtes agent, non?
Andréa Martel, je travaille chez ASK.
Vous ne devriez pas être au bureau?
En fait, je suis au travail là.
Je suis là pour vous. Vous êtes un talent rare.
Qu'est-ce que vous proposez exactement?
Je propose un nouvel élan artistique.
Tout ça est un peu bizarre.
Débarquer dans une salle de sport pour me parler!
Je suis chez Bréhier depuis trente-cinq ans.
On est un vieux couple. Je l'aime bien.
La nouveauté est un concept qui ne m'intéresse pas.
Peut-être que vous voulez juste vous ennuyer.
Ne dites pas du mal de l'ennui.
Je vous laisse donc vous ennuyer avec Bréhier.
Let's explore the conversation line by line and unpack the French phrases.
Bonjour, Fabrice! Tu viens souvent ici?
'Hello, Fabrice! Do you come here often?' Andrea initiates conversation with casual charm. The temporal adverb 'often' modifies the present tense question about routine attendance.
Je vous connais, vous êtes agent, non?
'I know you, you are an agent, right?' Luchini spots her professional identity immediately. The verb 'know' is used for recognizing or being acquainted with a person.
Andréa Martel, je travaille chez ASK.
'Andrea Martel, I work at ASK.' Andrea introduces herself with professional pride. The preposition 'at' denotes working at a particular company or agency.
Vous ne devriez pas être au bureau?
'Should you not be at the office?' Luchini raises an ironic eyebrow at her fitness location. The conditional verb 'should' expresses expectation or obligation in a polite register.
En fait, je suis au travail là.
'In fact, I am at work right now.' Andrea asserts that scouting him is official business. The discourse marker 'in' signals an unexpected clarification.
Je suis là pour vous. Vous êtes un talent rare.
'I am here for you. You are a rare talent.' Andrea delivers her direct flatteries. The adjective 'rare' follows the masculine noun 'talent' to convey exceptional distinction.
Qu'est-ce que vous proposez exactement?
'What are you offering exactly?' Luchini invites her specific commercial proposal. The interrogative phrase 'qu'est-ce que' asks what she proposes, sharpened by 'exactement'.
Je propose un nouvel élan artistique.
'I offer a new artistic impetus.' Andrea pitches fresh creative energy for his career. The masculine noun phrase 'a' uses the special masculine form 'new' before a vowel.
Tout ça est un peu bizarre.
'All of this is a bit strange.' Luchini comments on the theatrical ambush. The demonstrative pronoun 'all' is modified by the adjective 'strange'.
Débarquer dans une salle de sport pour me parler!
'Turning up in a gym to speak to me!' Luchini notes the comical unorthodoxy of the setting. The informal infinitive 'to show up' evokes showing up suddenly and unannounced.
Je suis chez Bréhier depuis trente-cinq ans.
'I have been with Brehier for thirty-five years.' Luchini reveals his deep agency history. The temporal preposition 'for' indicates an ongoing state that started in the past.
On est un vieux couple. Je l'aime bien.
'We are an old couple. I like him.' Luchini describes his relationship with his agent. The verb 'like him' expresses warm affection or fondness without romantic love.
La nouveauté est un concept qui ne m'intéresse pas.
'Novelty is a concept that does not interest me.' Luchini rejects trendy career shifts. The relative clause 'qui ne m'interesse pas' negates personal appeal emphatically.
Peut-être que vous voulez juste vous ennuyer.
'Maybe you just want to be bored.' Andrea challenges his resistance with witty sarcasm. The reflexive infinitive 'yourself' denotes experiencing boredom or dullness.
Ne dites pas du mal de l'ennui.
'Do not speak ill of boredom.' Luchini defends existential boredom as a creative state. The negative imperative 'not' forbids criticizing something.
Je vous laisse donc vous ennuyer avec Bréhier.

'I leave you then to be bored with Brehier.' Andrea concludes her exit with sharp wit. The verb 'leave' governs the reflexive infinitive 'yourself' in a graceful departure. Now let's listen to the entire dialogue once more to lock in what you have learned.

Andrea's bold fitness ambush ends with Luchini standing loyal to his long-time agent Brehier. Her pitch was spirited, but Luchini's love of familiar routine proved unshakeable.
Ne dites pas du mal de l'ennui.
